projectStructure.description: Project follows the Atomic Design methodology for component organization

fileNaming.description: File names use PascalCase component name followed by atomic level and .tsx extension

componentNaming.description: Component names use PascalCase with the atomic level as a suffix

atomicDesignLevels.molecules: Simple groups of atoms (search bar, form field)
atomicDesignLevels.organisms: Complex components made of molecules/atoms (header, footer, form)
atomicDesignLevels.pages: Specific instances of templates with real content

atomicDesignImplementation.overview: This project follows atomic design principles to ensure consistent, reusable, and maintainable UI components.

ButtonAtom.description: Uses Shadcn Button component for consistent styling and behavior. Always use ButtonAtom instead of raw HTML buttons.

DropdownAtom.description: Uses Shadcn Select component for consistent dropdown styling

DatePickerMolecule.description: Uses Shadcn Calendar and Popover components for enhanced date selection

noRawHTML.description: Never use raw HTML elements when atoms exist

createMissingAtoms.description: If you need a UI element that doesn't have an atom, create it

consistentSpacing.description: All admin pages should use px-6 for horizontal padding

cardUsage.pattern: <CardAtom><TextAtom variant="h3" weight="medium" className="mb-4">Section Title</TextAtom>{/* Section content */}</CardAtom>

hydrationSafety.description: Avoid nesting block elements inside TextAtom
hydrationSafety.solution: Use as="span" for inline text within list items or other inline contexts

uiFolderRestriction.description: NEVER create or modify components in src/components/ui/ folder
uiFolderRestriction.reason: The ui folder is reserved exclusively for Shadcn components installed via CLI
uiFolderRestriction.rule: Only use existing components from ui folder, never create new ones there
uiFolderRestriction.violation: Creating custom components in ui folder will break Shadcn component management

benefits: Consistency: All components follow the same design patterns
Maintainability: Changes to styling can be made in one place
Reusability: Components can be used across different pages
Type Safety: TypeScript interfaces ensure proper usage
Accessibility: Atoms can include built-in accessibility features
implementationChecklist: Replace all raw HTML elements with atoms
Use consistent spacing (mx-auto max-w-7xl for admin pages)
Use TextAtom for all text content
Use form atoms (InputAtom, SelectAtom, etc.) for forms
Use as="span" for inline text to avoid hydration issues

properAtomicDesignApplication.description: Don't put everything in pages - break down complex components into molecules and organisms

pages.responsibility: Should only orchestrate molecules and organisms, handle routing, and manage high-level state
pages.example: A page should import and compose molecules/organisms, not contain 300+ lines of JSX

molecules.responsibility: Groups of atoms that form a cohesive unit

namingConventions.descriptiveNames: Use descriptive names that clearly indicate the component's purpose
namingConventions.domainSpecific: Start with domain name if component is specific to that domain (e.g., Resident, CNA, etc.)
examples: ResidentBasicInformation.molecule.tsx - basic info specific to residents

organization.domainFolders: Create domain-specific folders inside molecules for better organization

characteristics: Reusable across different contexts (if generic) or domain-specific (if specialized)
Manages its own internal state if needed
Named descriptively to indicate exact purpose

organisms.responsibility: Complex components made of molecules and atoms
characteristics: May connect to external data sources

refactoringRules: If a page has 200+ lines, break it into molecules/organisms
If you see repeated patterns, extract them into molecules
If a component handles multiple concerns, split it
Each molecule should have a single responsibility
Molecules should be reusable and testable in isolation
